description: Cellular automata, Turing machines, substitution and string-rewriting systems and their visualizations, together with the curated datasets of polyhedra, graphs, lattices, knots, finite groups and related mathematical objects.

tools.name: CellularAutomaton
tools.description: Evolves a cellular automaton with a specified rule, initial condition and number of steps, in one or more dimensions. Rules can be given as Wolfram rule numbers, as {k, r} specifications or as explicit functions. It is the workhorse of computational-systems exploration.
tools.usage:
CellularAutomaton[rule, init, t]
CellularAutomaton[{n, {k, r}}, init, t]

parameters.name: rule
parameters.description: Rule number, {number, {colors, range}}, or a pure function of the neighborhood.

parameters.name: init
parameters.description: Initial row, or {{values}, background} for an infinite background.

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: Number of steps, or a step specification selecting which steps to return.

tools.example:
ArrayPlot[CellularAutomaton[30, {{1}, 0}, 200],
  ColorRules -> {0 -> White, 1 -> Black}, Frame -> False]
tools.notes: Two-dimensional automata such as the Game of Life use rule specifications like {224, {2, {{2, 2, 2}, {2, 1, 2}, {2, 2, 2}}}, {1, 1}}.

tools.name: RulePlot
tools.description: Draws a diagram of the rules of a cellular automaton, Turing machine or substitution system. It shows each case of the rule and its result graphically. Use it to document and explain a system's behaviour.

tools.name: TuringMachine
tools.description: Simulates a Turing machine with a given rule, initial state and tape, returning the evolution of head state, position and tape contents. Rules can be rule numbers or explicit transition lists. Use it for computability demonstrations and simple universal-computation experiments.
tools.usage:
TuringMachine[rule, init, t]
TuringMachine[{n, {s, k}}, init, t]
tools.notes: RulePlot[TuringMachine[n]] draws the transition table graphically.

tools.name: SubstitutionSystem
tools.description: Evolves a substitution system that repeatedly replaces elements according to given rules, in one or two dimensions. It generates fractals, L-system-like structures and self-similar patterns. Rules are given as ordinary replacement rules.
tools.notes: For geometric turtle-style systems, combine the generated string with Graphics primitives, or use AnglePath to trace the path.

tools.name: AnglePath
tools.description: Converts a sequence of turning angles, optionally with step lengths, into a list of 2D points tracing the resulting path. It is the standard way to draw turtle-graphics and L-system outputs. AnglePath3D does the same in three dimensions.

tools.name: PolyhedronData
tools.description: Provides data about hundreds of named polyhedra, including vertex coordinates, face structure, volume, surface area, symmetry group and images. Calling it with no arguments lists the available solids. Use it for geometry, crystallography and visualization.
tools.notes: PolyhedronData["Properties"] lists every available property; many polyhedra also provide "NetImage" for paper models.

tools.name: GraphData
tools.description: Gives data about thousands of named graphs, including their edge lists, spectra, chromatic numbers, planarity and standard embeddings. Classes such as "Cubic" or "Planar" list families of graphs. Use it for graph theory research and test cases.

tools.name: LatticeData
tools.description: Provides data about named lattices such as cubic, hexagonal and root lattices, including basis vectors, packing density, kissing number and images. It covers both crystallographic and abstract lattices. Use it for crystallography, coding theory and sphere packing.

tools.name: KnotData
tools.description: Gives data about knots and links, including crossing number, polynomial invariants, braid words and 3D embeddings. Knots are referenced by standard names such as "Trefoil" or Alexander-Briggs notation. Use it for knot theory and topological visualization.

tools.name: FiniteGroupData
tools.description: Provides data about finite groups, including order, generators, character tables, conjugacy classes and multiplication tables. Groups are named individually or by family such as {"SymmetricGroup", n}. Use it for algebra, representation theory and symmetry analysis.

tools.name: RandomInstance
tools.description: Generates a random instance of a symbolic geometric scene or other parameterized domain that satisfies its constraints. It is particularly useful with GeometricScene for exploring configurations. Several instances can be requested at once.
tools.example:
RandomInstance[GeometricScene[{a, b, c},
  {Triangle[{a, b, c}], EuclideanDistance[a, b] == EuclideanDistance[b, c]}]]

tools.name: GeometricScene
tools.description: Represents a symbolic geometric configuration defined by objects and constraints rather than explicit coordinates. Instances satisfying the constraints can be generated, and theorems about the scene can be found. Use it for synthetic geometry and automated theorem exploration.
tools.notes: FindGeometricConjectures searches for relations that hold across random instances of the scene.

tools.name: FindGeometricConjectures
tools.description: Searches for geometric relations such as equal lengths, concurrency or collinearity that appear to hold in a GeometricScene. It returns candidate conjectures ranked by plausibility. Use it as an exploratory tool in synthetic geometry.
